evals.prompt: Upgrade my films SolrCloud in namespace search from Solr 9.9 to 9.10 without downtime.
evals.expected_output: Runs or instructs scripts/preflight.sh first and restates the kube context for confirmation; checks replicationFactor >= 2 for every collection via cluster status; proposes the exact kubectl patch of spec.solrImage.tag but does not run it before approval; explains how to watch status.upToDateNodes/targetVersion and how to roll back.
expectations: Preflight (scripts/preflight.sh) is the first action and the kube context/namespace is restated for confirmation
Every collection's replicationFactor is checked, and RF 1 is called out as a query-gap risk
The kubectl patch command targets spec.solrImage.tag and is proposed, not executed, before user approval
Rollout completion is defined in terms of status.upToDateNodes reaching spec.replicas (and/or status.version == new tag)
A rollback path (patch the tag back) is stated
No Collections API call or solr-mcp tool is used to perform the upgrade

evals.prompt: shard2 of my films collection has been in recovering for over an hour. Cluster is films in namespace search. What's wrong and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Uses cluster status (get-cluster-status if solr-mcp has it, otherwise scripts/cluster-status.sh) to identify the replica and node; follows the incident runbook's recovering branch; checks disk and logs on that pod; proposes kubectl delete pod only if updateStrategy.method is Managed and the shard has another active replica; does not delete anything without approval.
expectations: Cluster status is obtained through the provider the capability map selects, not by guessing from pod phase
The specific replica and node from issues[] are named
Logs and disk usage on the affected pod are checked before any remedy
kubectl delete pod is only proposed with the stated conditions (Managed update strategy, another active replica), and is not executed without approval
ZooKeeper is checked if the node is missing from liveNodes

evals.prompt: I have a SolrCloud called films running in namespace search with basic auth on. Connect the Solr MCP server to it.
evals.expected_output: Follows runbooks/connect-mcp.md: uses scripts/mcp-values-from-cr.sh to derive SOLR_URL and the secret reference; chooses admin or a purpose-made solr-mcp user and explains why the bootstrapped solr user will not work for writes; never prints the password; verifies with tools/list and list-collections; warns about TLS trust if solrTLS is set.
expectations: Connection settings are derived from the CR via the script, not hand-typed
The bootstrapped 'solr' user is not chosen; admin or a dedicated solr-mcp user is, with the read-only reason stated
The password is never printed or base64-decoded into the conversation; the user is given the kubectl command to view it
Verification includes listing tools and calling list-collections against the running server

evals.prompt: Index this CSV of movies into my films collection.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill on a healthy connected cluster; that is solr-mcp's index-csv-documents or a plain Solr API task.
expectations: The skill is not loaded for a pure indexing task
